text: A casing? ...Alright. On the pile.
The bomber's coil. I've been after that for a month.
The honey. You went in the kitchen for the honey. ...Okay. Okay. Yard rule's complete.
Side door's open. I'm not making you pay for my door.
Crate's down by the hangar door. Don't say supply never gave you anything.
You want to be useful? My field radio's dead without its valve. There's a spare in the motor pool, in the parts box behind the second truck. Bring it here.
That's the one. Hold on... Range supply, this is the cage. One crate, hangar apron, now. ...They owe me. It's coming.
He'll ask nice. He always asks nice. He asked the Canaries nice.
Go on. I've got the range.
Go on. I've got the range, and a radio, and nothing goes to waste. That includes you. Come back.
You built it? The egghead's reactor, in a lantern? ...Course you did. Nothing on this range goes to waste.
That's Cal. That's... he was the first one. He went in the pit in August to see what it was. Shoot him in the rig. Please shoot him in the rig.
Generator's up. That's the lab lit. God help you, that's the lab lit.

...Say again? Say AGAIN. Is that... you're on the range? You're ALIVE on the range? Oh thank God. Oh thank... no, stay there. Don't come to the cage, it's crawling. I'm fine. I've got honey and a rifle.
Sergeant Marchetti. Supply. You're the first faces in three days that aren't trying to eat mine. ...British? And... Polish? Where in God's name did you fly in from?
That crate came in April. 'London.' The man in the office signed for it himself. He signs for everything himself.
That thing under the tarp hums at the Moon. I'm not being poetic. They pointed a dish at it. It hums back.
Those machines came with the crate. Olive drab's mine; I wasn't having violet in my hangar. The one with the lever, that's mine too. Don't drink it fast.
...range to capsule. Still here. Still answering.
...range to— you're on the Moon. I'm sitting in a cage in Nevada talking to the Moon.
...whatever you're about to do up there. Do it. I'll hear it from here.
